title: AICPA Statement of Position 82-1, Accounting and Financial Reporting for Personal Financial Statements; reprint
publisher: American Institute of Certified Public Accountants; reprint hosted by FASB
accounting_bases: Historical personal financial statement guidance underlying ASC 274; not a substitute for current Codification text
source_classification: Historical professional standard-setting guidance; source material identified by FASB as the basis for ASC 274
inspected_summary: The reprinted SOP addresses a statement of financial condition for an individual, spouses, or a family. It describes estimated current values for assets, estimated current amounts for liabilities, current-year income taxes payable, and an estimated tax provision on applicable differences between statement amounts and tax bases as if assets were realized and liabilities liquidated at the statement date. It calls for disclosure of methods and assumptions, limits jointly held property to the reporting person's beneficial interest under applicable property law, and says to show a substantial going-concern business interest as one amount rather than combine the separate entity's assets/liabilities with personal items.
locators: Physical PDF p. 2, paragraphs .03-.06; p. 3, paragraphs .07-.11; p. 4, paragraphs .12-.17; paragraphs .29-.32; illustrative paragraphs .34-.35

evidence.method: Direct original-source PDF open and page/paragraph reads
evidence.observed: Read the reporting-entity description, personal statement measurements, beneficial-interest rule, separate presentation of substantial business interests, current tax payable, estimated taxes on value-versus-tax-basis differences, assumptions/disclosures, and the provision directing application of other GAAP where appropriate.

access_limits: Historical SOP text, not a direct reading of current ASC 274. Selected pages only; the later Codification text and any subsequent changes were not fully inspected. No full text is stored.
effective_dates_and_supersession: Issued in 1982 and subsequently incorporated into the personal-financial-statement topic. Current wording and amendments must be checked in ASC 274; the SOP is not asserted to be current Codification text.
rights: AICPA retains its rights; the hosting URL does not establish permission to reuse. Only bibliographic metadata and a factual summary are stored.

title: Handbook: Consolidation
accounting_bases: US GAAP, ASC 810; ASC 946 scope exception as cross-referenced
source_classification: Professional-firm technical interpretation with reproduced Codification excerpts and examples
inspected_summary: The handbook describes the ASC 810 variable-interest-entity and voting-interest-entity models. For a VIE it explains the primary-beneficiary power and potentially significant economics tests. It reproduces the ASC 810-10-15-12(d) investment-company scope exception and explains that an investment company may still consolidate certain service entities, while investment companies remain subject to ASC 810 analysis when evaluated by another reporting entity.

evidence.method: Direct KPMG original PDF open and section/page reads

title: Roadmap: Fair Value Measurements and Disclosures, chapter 2, NAV practical expedient
accounting_bases: US GAAP, ASC 820; ASC 946 eligibility cross-reference
source_classification: Professional-firm fair-value roadmap reproducing ASC 820 text; secondary source, not the standard setter publication
inspected_summary: The roadmap reproduces ASC 820-10-15-4 and 35-59 through 35-62. It describes eligible investments without readily determinable fair value, consistent application to the whole position (subject to the stated probable-sale exception), and NAV consistent with ASC 946 as of the investor's measurement date. If latest NAV is not current to that date or not ASC 946-consistent, the investor considers whether an adjustment is needed to arrive at reporting-date NAV.
locators: DART Roadmap August 2026, §2.2.2, lines 142-175; ASC 820-10-15-4 and 35-59 through 35-62; Roadmap landing page lines 99-118 identifies the August 2026 edition

evidence.method: Direct DART Roadmap chapter open and paragraph/text read
evidence.observed: Read the eligibility, consistent application, date alignment and adjustment considerations, including the rule for a probable sale at a different amount. Deloitte's August 2026 landing page states no significant change from its 2025 edition.

access_limits: Secondary reproduction/explanation of Codification text; not a direct FASB source review or professional opinion. The page does not support an automatic adjustment for every stale NAV. No full text is stored.
effective_dates_and_supersession: Deloitte Roadmap edition dated August 2026; paragraph-level current Codification changes should be checked for the reporting date.
rights: Deloitte retains publication rights. DART identifies its Codification reproductions as made with FASB permission; that does not establish permission for this corpus to reuse the publication. No full text is stored.

title: 17 CFR 275.202(a)(11)(G)-1, Family offices
publisher: Electronic Code of Federal Regulations; U.S. Government Publishing Office and Office of the Federal Register
publication_date_or_edition: Current eCFR text displayed through 2026-09-22; retrieved 2026-09-24
accounting_bases: Federal investment-adviser regulation; not US GAAP or an accounting-perimeter rule
source_classification: Current federal regulation in eCFR; eCFR labels itself authoritative but unofficial
inspected_summary: The current displayed rule excludes a qualifying family office from the Advisers Act definition of investment adviser if it serves only defined family clients, is wholly owned by family clients, is exclusively controlled by family members or family entities, and does not hold itself out publicly as an investment adviser. It defines eligible family-client categories and includes a one-year treatment for certain involuntary transfers and grandfathering provisions.
